cf.title: MERGE fails to reject source references in NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE actions

input.subject: MERGE fails to reject source references in NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE actions

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal or the design: the patch makes an unaliased join source follow the rule that a single-table source already follows. The one surviving objection, standards-compat-1, is a fixable back-patch question that a committer who knows the MERGE parser must decide. Confidence is low because only message #1 exists and the code was not read.

brief.title: Reject source references in MERGE NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE when source is a join
brief.problem: MERGE accepts references to source relations in NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE actions when the USING source is an unaliased join. Postgres rejects the same reference when USING names a single table. The query from the report returns "MERGE 0" with no error, so a user can write an action that can never see source rows.
brief.proposed_design: setNamespaceForMergeWhen() hides only the top-level source RTE, so the input relations of an unaliased join stay visible by name. The patch restricts the namespace for each action by its match kind and restores it afterwards, as transformJoinOnClause() does. It uses the complete source namespace so the visibility rules from transformFromClause() for join inputs and aliases stay the same.
user_visible_surface: MERGE with an unaliased join source now raises "invalid reference to FROM-clause entry" for source references in NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE UPDATE expressions.
The same error now applies to source references in WHEN conditions of NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE actions.
author_claims: Source references in NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE actions should be rejected whether USING is a single table or an unaliased join.
Source references in WHEN conditions are also accepted by mistake today.
The fix keeps the source visibility flags set by transformFromClause().
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible. No one has replied.
unclear: The author does not say which released branches have the bug or whether the fix should be back-patched.
The proposal does not say whether an aliased join, a subquery or nested joins in USING behave correctly before and after the patch.
The proposal does not say whether NOT MATCHED BY TARGET actions now see the same namespace as before, for example target references.
Back-patching would make queries that run today fail, and the author does not discuss this.

objections.title: Back-patch policy for newly rejected MERGE queries is not stated
objections.failure_scenario: An application runs a MERGE with an unaliased join source that references a source column in a NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE action. After a minor-release update, that MERGE fails with "invalid reference to FROM-clause entry". The user finds out when the batch job errors in production.
objections.argument: The patch turns queries that parse and run today into parse errors, and it is tagged as a bugfix. Message #1 does not say which branches have the bug or whether the fix goes back. Rejecting these queries on master is consistent with the single-table case. On a stable branch, a committer would likely weigh the error against the current silent behaviour, where the source column has no matching source row and so cannot hold a source value.
objections.author_must_show: Which branches should get this fix, and how does it weigh breaking running queries on a minor update against the silent result those queries give today?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 and the commit message name no branches and do not discuss back-patching, yet the patch makes queries that run today fail at parse time. The scenario is concrete and tied to this change, and a statement from the author would answer it, so it stays fixable.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The patch changes which MERGE statements with a join source pass parse analysis; it adds no syntax.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The entry is tagged Bugfix, and a back-patch would make MERGE statements that run today fail at parse time.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which released branches accept these source references today, and do you propose to back-patch the fix or apply it to master only?
If back-patched, how do you weigh a new parse error on a minor update against the result these MERGE statements give today?
How do an aliased join, a subquery and nested joins in USING behave before and after the patch?
Do NOT MATCHED BY TARGET and MATCHED actions see the same namespace after the patch as before, including target references?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows MERGE parse analysis and the parser namespace rules in transformFromClause() would have to own it; no one has replied to message #1.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the new namespace handling in parse_merge.c and, if back-patched, for any MERGE statement that starts to fail on a minor update.
committability.author_follow_up: No sign either way; the thread has only message #1.

priority.reason: The patch is small, touches only parse_merge.c and the merge regression test, and adds no user-visible surface beyond an error. It affects only MERGE with an unaliased join source and a NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE action.

provisional_note: Without the code, it cannot be checked that the per-action namespace is restored on every path, or that aliased joins, subqueries, nested joins and NOT MATCHED BY TARGET actions keep their current behaviour.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert MERGE patch
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert MERGE patch
Reverted commit(s): MERGE SQL Command following SQL:2016; New files for MERGE; Improve parse representation for MERGE; MERGE syntax diagram correction; Allow cpluspluscheck to pass by renaming variable
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commits d204ef63776b8a00ca220adec23979091564e465,
83454e3c2b28141c0db01c7d2027e01040df5249 and a few more commits thereafter
(complete list at the end) related to MERGE feature.

While the feature was fully functional, with sufficient test coverage and
necessary documentation, it was felt that some parts of the executor and
parse-analyzer can use a different design and it wasn't possible to do that in
the available time. So it was decided to revert the patch for PG11 and retry
again in the future.

Thanks again to all reviewers and bug reporters.

precedents_retrieved.title: some namespace.c refactoring
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patches replace the repetitive per-object "is visible" and get_*_oid() functions in namespace.c with common code that uses objectaddress.c lookups for the syscache and attribute numbers of each catalog. Functions with special behavior were left unchanged.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane doubted that the patch preserves existing semantics and expected a performance penalty, and Alvaro Herrera pointed to the linear scan in get_object_property_data(). The author's own benchmark showed the "is visible" functions about 2 times slower in a tight loop, and his attempts to speed up get_object_property_data() helped little. Tom Lane did not answer the question about semantics in the visible messages. After almost a year without activity, vignesh C closed the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I have
very serious concerns first about whether it even preserves the
existing semantics, and second about whether there is a performance
penalty.

precedents_retrieved.title: COPY WHERE clause generated/system column reference
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patches make COPY FROM ... WHERE work with generated columns: they expand virtual generated columns in the WHERE clause and compute stored generated columns before the WHERE clause is checked. They also reject system columns other than tableoid in the WHERE clause.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut committed a smaller fix that rejects generated columns in COPY FROM WHERE with a clear error, and left tableoid for a separate thread. He then argued that support should not be added, because generated columns belong to the target table while the WHERE clause filters input data. Masahiko Sawada had shown that computing stored generated columns before the WHERE clause runs them before BEFORE INSERT triggers, so the WHERE clause changes the row the trigger sees.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This seems fundamentally wrong, because generated columns are a
property of the target table, but the COPY WHERE clause is meant to
filter the input data.

precedents_retrieved.title: possibility to rename root namespace in plpgsql
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a plpgsql compile option, `#routine_label new_name`, that gives the function's outer block a new label. A long function name then no longer has to be used to qualify arguments, for example `lnm.par1` in place of `very_long_name.par1`.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier found that the patch replaces the root label and changes the namespace lookup, and called this bug-prone. He found the later alias-based version still confusing in how it handles aliases across several layers of pl/pgsql. After months without progress, Julien Rouhaud saw no agreement on the patch or on the need for it, and Pavel Stehule, the author, agreed it should be rejected for lack of consensus.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
After a couple of months I see that there is unfortunately no agreement on this
patch, or even its need.

precedents_retrieved.title: Permute underscore separated components of columns before fuzzy matching
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend the fuzzy column-name matching behind the "Perhaps you meant" hint so that it also checks permutations of up to three underscore-separated words. A swap of two words costs the same as one mistyped character, and the permutation is skipped when the typed name has more than six underscores.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the patch adds opaque, almost undocumented code to the matching function, and he doubted that many users want this behavior. He also noted that adjacent underscores and leading or trailing underscores are not handled well. The visible messages show no reply from the author after this review, and the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
However, we *do*
need to be concerned about its maintainability, and I think the patch
falls down badly there: it adds a chunk of very opaque and essentially
undocumented code, that people will need to reverse-engineer anytime
they are studying this function.

precedents_retrieved.title: Range Merge Join
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend the existing Merge Join executor node to also handle range conditions (containment @> / <@ between a range and an element, or scalar BETWEEN-AND / paired inequalities), optionally combined with equality conditions, by adding a range_cond alongside the merge_cond and extending the merge join state machine. The planner would detect such conditions and use estimates to choose this "Range Merge Join" over other strategies.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tomas Vondra's review found that the patch still did not compile with asserts, had no regression tests exercising the new code, and lacked comments explaining the new functions and the reworked executor blocks. Two months later Julien Rouhaud asked whether the author planned to continue; no response from the author is visible before the entry was returned with feedback. Earlier, Jeff Davis had raised concerns about multiple join keys and suggested a CustomScan extension, which the authors declined.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I took a brief look at the patch, and I think there are two main issues
preventing it from moving forward.

precedents_retrieved.title: Indeterminate behavior for the GROUP BY clause
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Indeterminate behavior for the GROUP BY clause
Section: Features We Do Not Want
Linked: Re: SQL compatibility reminder: MySQL vs PostgreSQL
precedents_retrieved.objection: At least one other database product allows specification of a subset of the result columns which GROUP BY would need to be able to provide predictable results; the server is free to return any value from the group. This is not viewed as a desirable feature. PostgreSQL 9.1 allows result columns that are not referenced by GROUP BY if a primary key for the same table is referenced in GROUP BY.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix tab completion MERGE
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch improves psql tab completion for MERGE, adding WHEN [NOT] MATCHED, DO NOTHING and MERGE INTO completions and fixing wrong completions after AS. A second patch (0002) adds a PartialMatches() helper so the MERGE-specific rules apply only when MERGE appears earlier in the command.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The first patch (0001) was committed. Dean Rasheed reviewed 0002 in January 2023, questioned whether PartialMatches() was needed, and asked for a new name and code changes. No updated patch followed, so the commitfest managers returned the entry with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There are still no updates to this patch or thread, so I'm closing this as
Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Make selectivity example match wording
precedents_retrieved.summary: The doc patch changes the unique, non-null join selectivity example so that it divides by the maximum of the two row counts, as the prose describes, and uses num_rows in place of num_distinct. A v2 patch also rewrote the explanation of the formula in the docs and in the code comments, including the proof in the comments.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The reviewer called the smaller change valuable and was "good" apart from one wording suggestion. The thread then has no further messages before the entry was returned with feedback in November.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add pg_upgrade check for invalid role references in pg_init_privs
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a pg_upgrade check that finds pg_init_privs entries whose ACLs reference role OIDs that no longer exist in pg_authid. Today pg_upgrade --check passes such clusters, and the upgrade then fails when pg_restore grants privileges to the dropped role.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Only the opening message is shown, with no replies, and the entry was withdrawn ten days later.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: none of the 24 retrieved rows covers the same or a similar idea, and message #1 points to no earlier discussion. The patch makes MERGE with an unaliased join source match the single-table behaviour, so no earlier rejection reason applies.
From the standards and compatibility angle, the change aligns the join case with the existing single-table rule and adds no syntax, GUC or dumped object. The only open point is the back-patch policy.

The patch changes only parse-analysis namespace visibility in parse_merge.c plus regression tests. It touches no on-disk format, WAL, catalog, wire protocol or extension ABI, so nothing on this angle needs review. Stored rules or views cannot contain MERGE today, so no persisted parse trees are affected.

The patch only makes MERGE reject source column references in NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE actions when the source is a join. It does not change privileges, RLS, column privilege checks, or what data a user can see, and it adds no new resource use. So there is no security or privilege objection from this angle.

From the maintenance and fit angle there is nothing to object to. The patch is a parser bug fix in parse_merge.c that reuses the save-and-restore namespace pattern of transformJoinOnClause(), costs only parse time and adds no GUC, catalog or API. Without the code, two points cannot be checked: whether NOT MATCHED BY TARGET actions keep their namespace, and how aliased joins, subqueries and nested joins behave. No committer has replied yet, so no owner is known. Back-patching would make queries that run today fail; that question belongs to the compatibility angle.

This is a parser bug fix that makes an unaliased join source in MERGE behave like a single-table source, which already raises an error. No existing feature, extension or hook does this job, and the patch adds no new mechanism. Its namespace handling follows transformJoinOnClause(). Back-patch impact and coverage of aliased joins and subqueries belong to other angles.

This is a bug fix. It makes an unaliased join source behave like the single-table case, which Postgres already rejects, so the demand angle does not apply. Users and maintainers pay no new cost. The only open demand-related point is whether to back-patch, since queries that run today would start to fail. That is a compatibility question for other angles.
